content.label: Just recently started using things 3. It’s powerful and I’m now moving all reminders to things 3. The only thing I’d like to see is ability to assign some emoji or icon to areas. Great tool overall.

Things has been keeping me organized and up to date with my projects both big & small for many years now.

I would really love for the widget to display reminders that have one of the multiple tags im filtering for. It seems like a reminder requires having all of the tags I’m filtering for to show up on the widget.

This app kept me organized through the onslaught of assignments, clinicals, exams, and state deadlines for nursing school. It’s so intuitive and beautifully designed! It makes my brain happy to use it, it is minimal. Thank you for the obvious care put into each little feature!
Having tried many other popular todo apps, Things 3 remains the defacto

title.label: Easy way to Organize your day

content.label: Top notch app

title.label: Love the app; Hate the Clear button

content.label: The title pretty much says it. Why the devs thought we need a gigantic clear button is beyond me. Bump it accidentally and — poof! — your entry is gone. I’ve seen a dev reply to a similar complaint here in another review, saying to the user, effectively, “you’re doing it wrong .” Umm, no, it’s a lousy interface choice.

I tried and gave up on things and all to do apps several years ago because I was spending more time creating my list than doing things.  I recently asked ChatGPT if there are any apps out there that solve my list of which in a nutshell was easy to manage and intuitive and things three came up.  I downloaded my previous version on my iPhone and even bought the $50 app for my MacBook Air and after a couple of days, I am so loving life!!!!

I really love things. I’ve tried several times to simplify my apps and use more default apple options but I keep coming back to things. The visual design keeps things simple and easy to manage but this doesn’t sacrifice functionality. Things packs a lot into a little. 

I finally completed the sample project. It’s well designed and practical. Gets you up and running quick. 

Great app! Thanks for all the work that went into it.

How do I use this app and for what purpose? I’m using Actions for everything as I’m paying yearly for the bundle and Apple Reminders for everything doing with managing my devices already as is. Any suggestions?

Still great, still supported (iOS26), really one of my most important tools.

Quick Entry would be fantastic to have with more supported apps (or as a screenshot taker).

I used Things 2 way back on OSX, and had my first experience with using a hotkey to bring up making new to-dos. Soon after I had to switch back to PC, and always missed Things. I knew it was a good app because it was the only application that tempted me to get an iPhone if I needed to upgrade. Now after many years and other to-do apps I have come back with Things, now in my pocket!

I recommend this app because it hides more nuanced features under a well-designed surface. I also recommend manually using the logbook and creating to-dos to cross them off soon after. This encourages the user to not overwhelm themselves with to-dos and instead encourages organization with the areas, projects and headers design elements they’ve created in Things. 

I would like an option to toggle the number of to-dos listed in the inbox and today when I am on the home-screen, please. That’s about all. Thank you for the app!

ios26 update they changed the Done button to Clear. This is absolutely terrible for those of us that have been using Things 3 since its inception. 

Who thought this change was a good idea? Fire that person.
I am using iOS26 and whenever I open the app, it crashes. Uninstalled and reinstalled, nothing. Works great on Macbook and iPad tho...
For my day to day work, it is unsurpassed. Rock solid stability and continuous advancement of UI are unique.  Just works, and works really, really well.!

For some reason, when setting reminders, the developers decided to change the “done” button to a “clear” (cancel) button. So now I set a bunch of reminders that I’ll never get notifications about because my usual pattern (setting the reminder) is now the opposite (clearing the reminder). Idiotic stuff.

I love Things. It’s the perfect balance of powerful features, simplicity, and beautiful UI. As my needs change, it’s easy to adapt how I use things to support really complex or incredibly simple workflows. I also appreciate how quick Things is at adopting new OS features - it keeps the app feeling fresh. I’ve bought the apps for iPhone, iPad, and Mac. And, I would welcome the change to pay a small subscription fee on top of that to support what I’m sure is the ongoing development expense of thoughtfully keeping the apps up to date with the latest & greatest OS features. Thanks for building great software and making my life easier 🙏🏼.

title.label: IPAD Magic Keyboard Interface link issue

content.label: I have engaged the Cultured Code team about an issue where the keyboard will randomly lose connection for specific buttons (return, CMD, etc). They stated that it is an apple problem but this is the only app this occurs in. If this issue is resolved. I will update to 5 stars because the app is great otherwise.

I was able to benefit immediately from this app with just a few minutes of use. I continue to learn about new features that I find useful. By far the best app I have found for task management, with great calendar management, and useful for simple project management too.

Really not a fan of the new Glass UI update they made. To me, it doesn't really make any sense. Things was always an app that was distinctive in its approach to its user interface, acting like virtual paper that separated and expanded. To be honest, the user interface follows principles more similar to Google's Material Design in that fashion. They kind of just shoehorned all of this new rounded shiny UI into the app, and it breaks the magic that they had. It looks tacky.

Okay, so, I am a list maker. I’ve always preferred writing lists down physically on paper. But, lately I’ve been wishing for a better way to keep track of multiple projects, areas, lists, and sublists in one spot. I googled “best to do list app” and was not disappointed. I’ve been using Todoist for a while and even paid for the subscription. It worked, but just didn’t do exactly what I wanted it to.  Today, yes I am reviewing the app immediately-something I never do, I was not disappointed. In reviewing the app specifications and recognizing it as a one-time charge I downloaded it immediately. I went through the handy “Meet Things” project and was thrilled with the basics, every single question/desire that came up as I started my own lists, projects, and areas was answered and given. It is obvious that a lot of thought and effort went in to this application. I honestly am so thrilled! Thank you to the developers!
I’ve tried so many other todo apps, none come close to Things 3.

TLDR: find another app. I was a power user with things, but it no longer fits my needs. 

I never thought I’d write this. Things has always been the best. Always the sharpest looking. Always ready for productivity. Always in Apple’s spotlight. But Things has been slowing down…

Today, iOS 26 launched. I woke up hopeful that Things would surprise us by giving us a new feature. Maybe a new UI refresh. Nope. Their update was a barebones update to stay “current”. A glass icon and a glassy like plus button. Wooo thanks! 

I have bought every version of things. The visionOS release was strike one. A full price for a multi year app that just has translucent sidebars? Come on. I messaged the devs many times asking what most of us are asking and needing: attachment support, better markdown (the current setup is insanely stupid), collaboration, or even a refreshed coat of paint to not look like an older app. The responses we get? Thanks for the feedback, we aren’t doing it. 

Today, I’m uninstalling things. This big update from them is a joke. To the other devs who listen and keep the magic of Apple software release day still magical, thank you. To Cultured Code, thanks for the great years ranging all the way back to Things 1. You’ve lost your touch, your magic. I hope you find it again and find joy in your work.

I love this app. It’s probably the app I use the most - besides Messages and Safari. The UI is smoother than all the others and postponing tasks until the evening is a game-changer. It’s only missing a quick-list or a ‘starred’ list. I have hundreds of things on my list every day but sometimes I just want to choose a handful at a time to tackle and tags just aren’t practical.

While Things appears to be the most solid to do app, and one I’ve used for years, there is still room for improvement to make it more intuitive. 

I use a lot of recurring reminders, and each time have to look up how to make them recur in the app. I don’t have this issue with any other app, but Things makes it hard to do, there’s no clear way to make a reminder recurring, instead you have go to to one you already created and find the right place to press to make it recurring. If you have a long task name, you cannot easily get to the exact place to click to make a task recurring.

To make this more intuitive, it would be far more helpful if users could make a task recurring upon creation in the same area where we set the time or date reminder. It would make  most sense to then be able to set the reminder to be recurring, but that’s not how it works on the app. 

Please make this easier and more intuitive, as this would greatly improve the user experience.

title.label: App crashing on new ios beta

content.label: I can’t open the app anymore, but it did work fine in this beta for 2-3 weeks, no issues.

I need REPEATED daily tasks. Pointless app if it doesn’t do that. It’s also ATROCIOUS to find out that if I want it on my laptop I have to pay another $50????? I would really like a refund. I’ll stick to notion.

content.label: I have been using Things 3 for years and it has been working well and very helpful. I recently noticed if I use voice dictation to write my tasks, it won’t save, the second I hit enter or exit dictation mode, all the texts I just dictated disappear. Can this problem be fixed? Thank you.
We need a better dark mode icon asap

So many starts and stops with to-do apps through the years. Many of them have nice features, but they’ve always fizzled for me. So far, Things is the only one to keep me engaged in 10+ years of attempts. It is taking less and less time to use as I get better with the UI. I had to create a script to copy my work calendar to Google, then connect that to iOS calendar, and now I see all my daily meetings, color-coded, as well as all tasks and projects, all on the same phone screen, which is kind of incredible. Just set up daily health habits I can check off, which is my first major usage of checklists within the tasks - so helpful. Just wanted to say thank you.

I’ve used Things over the years. I loved what Things was trying to accomplish. But I was never quite happy with the product. This has changed with things 3! I love the subtle changes and the beautiful interface there’s always had so I’ve used it. Now Things 3, is out. I’ve used Things 3, a few times and I’ve decided to commit to it. Thank you very much for all your hard work on this product. For making it one of the best APPs in the industry.
I use it everyday to maintain my schedule and keep my ADHD in check. It’s actually fun to tic off those to-dos!

There is no way to refund this app, somebody described this as a frustrating experience and couldn’t find more accurate words. This app doesn’t integrate well with any enterprise grade ecosystem. It could potentially work for you if you lived in a remote island by yourself but even then you couldn’t install it and get a refund! Keep your money in your pocket and try other alternatives before dropping 60 bucks on this app (mac + iPhone)

title.label: This has an app notification badge!!!!

content.label:
What I need MOST from any reminder app is an “in your face” alert that something needs to be done today.

Having a little number on the corner of the app icon when there are undone tasks works PERFECTLY for me, but apps generally don’t describe whether they have it or not.

So I held my breath when I bought this. But guess what — THERE’S A NOTIFICATION BADGE!

I win!

PS: Devs, please mention this in the app description!!
I think that this is the best task management app there is available!

I’ve been using the 2Do app for MANY years. I have tried out many other productivity apps over the years but always came back to 2Do. One of the main items I’ve been looking for in another app is the ability to put a start and stop date like 2Do, but can also do some of the newer features like add a todo with Siri. 
Things 3 is working great! I can add a deadline for items that I can do in a week or month. I like how easy it is to move a todo item to the next day - So I only see what a truly plan to do today.  And I that I can add a todo from my email or with Siri! I also like the Someday list that I look at when I have some spare time (or extra energy!)
You should give a preview or a free trial, because I would not have bought the app if I had been able to try it beforehand and that it wouldn’t work for me.

I love a good todo app, and what I always look for is one that carries my un-dones forward. Things3 does this, and so much more. A real bonus for me is the Project management aspect. My to-do can sprout baby to-dos underneath, so all the pieces of the work are organized and accessible in one view. 
And there is more to still discover.

I used Things as my do-everything app, from 2019 to 2025. I’m moving to Todoist because I need a bit more features / functions, but things is GREAT for 95% of people and I will sing its praises forever.
I am no longer able to have the list feature on the front screen(the most beneficial feature) of my apple watch ultra 2

title.label: No export functionality, you are locked in

content.label:
Have been using Things for years and liked it. However, just had the worst experience trying to move away from it due to switching to an android phone. While platforms like todoist give you the option to export tasks, Things doesn’t and makes it as hard as possible to move your data out of their system. They give you a database file where half of information is missing such as projects, recurring reminders, etc. In the end I spent days getting a spreadsheet of my information and had to manually go through hundreds of records to update them. 
Unfortunately, I can no longer recommend them.

title.label: CONTINUALLY CRASHING // CANNOT EVEN OPEN TONSEE MY TO DO’S

content.label:
I literally can’t even open the app because the second I do, it completely crashes. 

This issue started on my iPad and now on my iPhone. 

Thing is that there is NO way to access on a browser. This is not a good back up option. Especially when the app goes down. 

This is devastating. I’m in the middle of so many projects and everything is in this app. 

I am trying to figure out how to move everything to a more reliable app. 

Really disappointing. 

If you can’t be without your to-do list, I’d highly suggest a platform with a back up web browser.

The placement and sensitivity of the blue plus button in the bottom right corner is an endless source of frustration. I’ve brought this up to you for years but you seem not to care. The rest of the app works so well, that simply moving this button would make it nearly perfect. The problem is if you swipe up anywhere near it, you inadvertently add a new item, and to make matters worse, there’s no delete option in its initial pop-up. You’re forced to accept it and then re-open it to delete it. And the suggestion from a staff member before to scroll higher up in the app doesn’t work when you swipe up to exit the app and as you exit it adds a blank to do item that I have to delete later.

Cultured code delivers in performance and beauty with Things 3 but, one real issue I have is when setting a date or when I’m going to do a certain task the calendar pops up I choose the date then it goes away, I have to select again to then sent the time of my reminder. I thought this was a bug it’s not, it’s how they designed it. Makes no sense. Let me choose a date and reminder time then give me the option to press done when I’m actually done. Maybe make this process optional in settings??

Things three really fulfills all my needs. I need more flexibility than Apple Reminders. Things 3 works for all my devices and all my needs. One of the best features is that you don’t need a huge amount of documentation because the app is very intuitive.

title.label: Best todo app (I’ve tried them all)

content.label:
This app is extremely well designed and implemented. Bonus, it works well with the GTD system.

Accessibility ask:

One thing I would like is the ability to move the + button (to add tasks) from the right side to the left. The button is so small, and it’s difficult to use with the left hand.

Have been using this app daily for about a year, it’s a lifesaver for business owners, and even people who want a to do list, that’s simple, clean, and effective.

Highly recommend 💎🤝

I’ve been a long-time user of Things and really appreciate the clarity and design of the app. It’s a great middle ground between a simple reminders app and a gtd system. 

One small but meaningful improvement I’d love to see is the ability for recurring tasks to automatically reappear in the “This Evening” section of Today, rather than defaulting to the general Today list.

Currently, I have to manually move recurring tasks into “This Evening” every time they regenerate, which adds friction to an otherwise smooth workflow. It would be incredibly helpful if the app remembered a task’s last placement or allowed me to designate “This Evening” as its default.

Thanks for all your thoughtful work on Things—I’d be excited to see this added in a future update.
Was fine before update please fix
